body.estimand_functional: \(\theta(P)=\theta_b(P_O)\text{ for }P\in\mathcal M_b,\ b\in\{\mathrm{PT},\mathrm{SC}\};\quad\) at each explicitly strict-interior constant-rank intersection theorem point \(P_0\), \(\phi_U(P_0)=\chi_0+\sum_x\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}=\chi_0+\sum_x\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\}\), where the centered coefficients solve \(\mathrm{QP}_x\). The equality identifies the causal ATT branchwise; the union gradient and its sharpness are local to the displayed strict-interior subclass.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a fixed-length micro panel with finite group and covariate supports.
sampling_model.treatment: Group one is untreated through \(T-1\) and treated only in period \(T\); every donor group remains untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \( (G,X) \) cell obeys the weak model margins. The tangent, envelope, adaptation, and endpoint theorems are evaluated only at intersection laws with strict cell-mass and two-sided conditional-group-probability slack, strict fourth-moment and SC-rank slack, a strict positive-normal-eigenvalue gap, and locally constant Gram rank.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The treated-stratum probabilities \(\nu_x\), conditional contrasts \(C_b(x)\), centered contrast gradients \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\), normalized restriction gradients, and covariance Grams are finite-dimensional observed-law objects for strict-interior lower-bound and adaptation calculations. SunXieZhang2025 instead analyzes one integrated estimator and one multiplier construction under alternative PT and SC hypotheses, with branch-specific influence functions and variances. The present branch-chart extension includes branch-specific \(\chi_b(P)\) off the intersection. No cross-fitted projection estimator, variance estimator, data-driven chart coupling, or multiplier procedure is proved valid over the frozen local-sequence class.

The PT condition is donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. The SC identification condition uses covariate-indexed weights shared across periods, summing to one with negative weights allowed and \(T\ge J\); its regular SC analysis uses a nonsingular reference-donor difference system equivalent to full column rank of augmented \(B\).

Section 3 studies local efficiency for a different finite-support union model, not the strict-interior PT--SC ATT tangent geometry here.
Proposition 1(a), equation (2.11), gives the two-group panel-DiD ATT efficient influence function, and equation (2.12) gives its efficiency bound; equation (2.13) concerns repeated cross-sections.
Its cross-fit remainder theory is guidance for a repaired theorem with common rate control; it does not validate finite-coordinate-spliced sequence uniformity.
Its branchwise-drift analysis is guidance for a repaired theorem but does not remove the frozen class's finite-coordinate-splicing obstruction.

body.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification is valid on the union of conditional parallel trends and a full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction. At explicitly strict-interior constant-rank intersection laws, the corrected derivative separates the treated-composition gradient \(\chi_b\) from conditionally centered contrast gradients \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\). The common composition term is orthogonal to the centered PT and SC faces, so the local union convolution bound is \(E[\chi_0^2]\) plus finite covariance-weighted program values, and observable Gram discrepancies characterize simultaneous and one-sided oracle adaptation. The exact three-group gaps and the single- and saturated-donor endpoints remain unchanged under this repaired scope. This is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark on the strict-interior subclass; it transfers by restriction to estimators regular over the broader published union but supplies no attaining estimator or inference. Finite-coordinate splicing makes uniform one-step, variance, and multiplier validity false over the frozen sequence class.

project_justification.gap: SunXieZhang2025 studies one integrated estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction under alternative PT and SC hypotheses, obtaining branch-specific influence functions and asymptotic variances; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives PT efficiency alone. Neither source determines the common regular influence class or convolution bound for the nonnested union after separating treated composition from centered conditional-mean variation, and neither supplies the strict-interior oracle-adaptation tests proved here.
project_justification.niche: Finite covariate support turns each branch into finitely many conditional-mean restrictions. At strict-interior constant-rank intersection points, two-sided tangent paths are valid, \(\chi_b\) separates from \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\), and the common \(\chi_0\) is orthogonal to the centered restriction geometry. The resulting efficiency loss and adaptation frontier are computable from observed conditional covariance Grams.
project_justification.fill: The project characterizes the corrected PT and SC affine influence classes at explicitly strict-interior constant-rank intersection laws, solves their centered intersection by stratum covariance-weighted quadratic programs, and adds \(E[\chi_0^2]\) to the union and oracle variances. It proves simultaneous and one-sided oracle criteria, the strict three-group region, and both endpoint reductions. The envelope is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark on this subclass and transfers to broader-union regular estimators only by restriction. It is not an implemented standard error. The frozen sequence class cannot support the requested uniform one-step and multiplier theorem because it permits arbitrary finite-coordinate splicing.

body.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor and studies one integrated estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction under alternative PT and SC hypotheses, with branch-specific influence functions and asymptotic variances. Its PT condition is donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. Its SC hypothesis uses covariate-indexed weights common across periods, summing to one with negative weights allowed and \(T\ge J\); the intercept row of \(B\) encodes the sum constraint. Its identification theorem need not identify weights uniquely, while its regular SC estimation analysis assumes a uniformly nonsingular reference-donor difference system equivalent, after reparameterization, to full column rank of augmented \(B\). The present model is a finite-support, uniform-overlap, uniform-moment, full-rank subclass, and sharpness is further local to explicitly strict-interior constant-rank theorem points. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting but not the nonnested union geometry. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different union model. SantAnnaZhao2020, Proposition 1(a), equation (2.11), supplies the panel-DiD influence function recovered when \(J=1\), and equation (2.12) supplies its efficiency bound; equation (2.13) is repeated cross-section. Newey1990, Sections 2--3, supports the generic regular-estimator efficiency lower bound, while Newey1994 is retained only for its separately verified constant-rank role. NeweyRobins2018, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016, and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 are guidance for a possible theorem on a redesigned uniform neighborhood. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer by restriction to estimators regular over the broader published union, but no implemented inference transfers from the present results. RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska analysis in SunXieZhang2025 motivate the benchmark.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The union envelope is a regularity lower bound only at explicitly strict-interior constant-rank intersection laws: every path-relevant support, fourth-moment, SC-rank, positive-normal-eigenvalue, and, where used, local-score-variance inequality has strict slack. Boundary points, rank changes, vanishing overlap, changing support, covariance degeneracy, and weight-boundary restrictions require different local experiments. The common treated-composition component is identified analytically, but no attaining estimator, usable standard error, or multiplier-confidence procedure is established. The negative theorem exploits the frozen sequence class's closure under arbitrary finite-coordinate replacement and does not settle a redesigned common neighborhood with common QMD, score, and remainder bounds.
body.honest_scope: The proved deliverables, all at explicitly strict-interior constant-rank intersection laws, are the corrected tangent-normal characterization \(\mathcal I_b=\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}R_b\), the finite centered union convolution lower bound with \(E[\chi_0^2]\), observable oracle-adaptation tests, the exact three-group witness with strict fourth-moment slack, and the single- and saturated-donor reductions. Sharpness is local to this subclass. The lower bound and the finite-coordinate-splicing impossibility transfer to estimators regular over the broader published union only by restriction. The results provide a benchmark, not an implemented estimator, standard error, or confidence interval. The frozen local-sequence class makes a single uniformly chartwise asymptotic-linear expansion, and hence the requested one-step, variance-consistency, and multiplier-coverage theorem, false. No positive sequencewise continuation theorem is claimed.
